name: Seated Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
movementSteps: Sit comfortably with the working foot resting on a board beneath an elastic band affixed to that board.
Set a physical stop where the working foot reaches its comfortable lifted position.
Begin from the self-selected resting position with the sole on the board, and hold the selected knee posture still.
Lift the front of the foot toward the shin until it reaches the stop, without turning the foot inward or outward or lifting through the toes alone.
Return under control until the sole touches the board, then repeat before changing sides.

name: Standing Unilateral Machine Calf Raise
movementSteps: Stand in a single-leg calf-raise machine with the front of the working foot centered on the platform and your shoulder beneath the load pad.
Keep the working knee straight and hold your hips, back, knee, and foot steady.
Raise the heel as high as you can, then lower under control without bending the knee or curling the toes.

name: Seated Unilateral Machine Calf Raise
movementSteps: Sit in a single-leg calf-raise machine with the front of the working foot centered on the platform and the lower thigh beneath the load pad.
Keep the working knee bent near 90 degrees and hold the hip, pelvis, back, knee, and foot still.
Raise the heel as high as you can, then lower under control without straightening the knee or curling the toes.

name: Stable Forearm Plank
movementSteps: Place both forearms on a stable floor with your elbows below your shoulders and your upper arms pointing straight down.
Support the lower body on both feet and align the spine, pelvis, hips, and knees in one neutral straight line.
Hold this position for the set time without letting your lower back sag.
Keep the hold still without turning it into a crunch, hip lift, reach, or limb movement.

name: Side Plank
movementSteps: Lie on one side and support your body on that forearm, with both your shoulder and elbow at about 90 degrees.
Straighten both legs, place the top foot in front of the lower foot, and place the free hand on the opposite shoulder.
Lift your body into a straight line from shoulder through hip to feet.
Hold your body still for the set time without dipping your hips or moving your arms or legs.
Repeat the hold on the other side.

name: Feet-Together Band Pallof Hold
movementSteps: Attach a band to a side pulley so its line of pull is horizontal, then stand side-on with the feet together on a stable floor and hold the handle in both hands at shoulder height.
Straighten both elbows until your arms point directly forward, and choose a tension you can control.
Hold for the set time without letting your torso or hips turn, and do not repeatedly press your arms in and out.
Repeat with the anchor on the other side.

name: Barbell Back Squat
movementSteps: Stand with your heels about hip-width apart and a straight barbell resting securely across your upper back.
Hold the bar with both hands in an overhand grip, brace your torso, and keep both feet planted.
Bend your hips and knees, letting your knees travel forward naturally, until your upper thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive through both feet and straighten your hips and knees to return to standing while keeping the bar controlled.
Do not sit on a box, bounce at the bottom, or deliberately round or arch your back to complete the repetition.

name: Barbell Front Squat
movementSteps: Stand with your heels about hip-width apart and support a straight barbell across the front of your shoulders and collarbones in a clean grip.
Brace your trunk, keep your elbows lifted, and keep both feet planted.
Bend your hips and knees, letting your knees travel forward naturally, until your upper thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive through both feet and straighten your hips and knees to return to standing while keeping the bar balanced on the front of your shoulders.
Do not sit on a support, bounce at the bottom, or deliberately round or arch your back to complete the repetition.

name: Flat Dumbbell Fly
movementSteps: Lie on your back on a flat bench with one dumbbell over each shoulder, your palms facing each other, and your elbows held in a fixed slight bend.
Lower the upper arms outward at shoulder height.
Sweep your upper arms together until the dumbbells meet over your chest without pressing, changing the elbow bend, or deliberately reaching your shoulder blades forward.

name: Standing Band Fly
movementSteps: Stand between the anchored ends of an elastic band with the upper arms held at shoulder height, the palms facing inward, and the elbows in a fixed slight bend.
Brace your torso and sweep your upper arms together until your hands meet in front of your chest.
Return under control without pressing, changing the elbow bend, or deliberately reaching your shoulder blades forward.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Secure the legs on a bench declined 15 degrees, and lie with the eyes below the racked bar.
Lower the bar under control toward the lower-chest line.
Press the bar up until your elbows are straight while keeping your torso and shoulders supported.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Secure the legs on a bench declined 15 degrees, and begin with one dumbbell beside each lower-chest line.
Keep each forearm beneath its dumbbell, and press upward and slightly inward until your elbows are straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control without turning the repetition into a fly.

name: Decline Smith Machine Bench Press
movementSteps: Set a decline bench to 15 degrees, and position it so the Smith bar descends toward the lower chest without forcing the shoulders forward.
Lower the bar along the rails under control.
Press until your elbows are straight while keeping your torso and shoulders supported.

name: Decline Machine Chest Press
movementSteps: Adjust the seat so the handles begin beside the lower chest and follow an approximately 15-degree downward path relative to a horizontal press.
Keep your torso against the pad, and press the handles forward and inward until your elbows are straight.
Return under control.

name: Seated 45-Degree Cable Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit on a flat bench facing a high cable with both feet on the floor and no thigh restraint.
Hold the straight bar wider than shoulder width with your palms facing forward, straighten your elbows, and point your arms upward at about 45 degrees.
Keep your head straight and your core tight as you pull the bar to your chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Allow your shoulder blades to move naturally instead of deliberately pinching or rotating them.
Return slowly to the same 45-degree start without pulling your arms across your body, twisting, leaning to propel the bar, or using your lower body.
Log the cable weight you actually use rather than the suggested starting weight of 35 lb or 15 kg; this exercise was tested with weights equal to 10% and 25% of body weight.

name: Bar Dip
movementSteps: Support the full body above fixed dip bars with no foot contact.
Bend your elbows and lower under control only as far as feels comfortable, letting your upper arms move slightly behind your torso.
Press back up until your elbows are straight without swinging, kicking, or forcing your shoulder blades into a specific position.

name: Ring Dip
movementSteps: Support the full body above two independent rings with no foot contact.
Keep the rings controlled beside your torso as you bend your elbows and lower only as far as feels comfortable, letting your upper arms move slightly behind you.
Press back up until your elbows are straight without kipping or using your legs.

name: Bodyweight Forward Lunge
movementSteps: Stand upright with both feet supporting you and cross your arms over your upper body.
Step forward with the selected lead foot and land with the whole foot in contact.
Lower under control for three seconds to your full self-selected depth.
Keep the lead foot planted as you straighten the lead hip and knee and rise toward standing over two seconds.
Step the lead foot back beside the other foot to complete the repetition.
Finish the set on the selected side, then repeat with the other lead leg.

name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
movementSteps: Stand upright with both feet supporting you and cross your arms over your upper body.
Keep the selected front foot planted and step the opposite foot backward.
After the rear foot lands, lower under control for three seconds to your full self-selected depth without moving the selected front foot.
Straighten the selected front hip and knee and rise toward standing over two seconds.
Bring the rear foot forward beside the front foot.
Finish the set with the same selected front leg, then repeat on the other side.

name: Single-Arm Supinated Cable Triceps Pushdown
movementSteps: Stand at a high cable, and hold a single handle with the working palm facing up.
Keep the upper arm alongside your torso and the wrist straight as you straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
Return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Pronated Cable Triceps Pushdown
movementSteps: Stand at a high cable, and hold a single handle with the working palm facing down.
Keep the upper arm alongside your torso and the wrist straight as you straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
Return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
movementSteps: Stand with one arm overhead and the palm facing up while the cable pulls against you.
Keep your upper arm, wrist, torso, and lower body still as you straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
Return under control.

name: Seated Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
movementSteps: Sit upright without back support, and hold one dumbbell overhead with your palm facing inward.
Keep your upper arm and torso still as you bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell.
Straighten the elbow as far as you can without turning the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
movementSteps: Lie on your back on a bench with one dumbbell held over your chest, your palm facing inward, and your upper arm pointing straight up.
Hold your upper arm still, and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell.
Straighten the elbow as far as you can.

name: Supinated Straight-Bar Cable Curl
movementSteps: Stand facing a low cable while holding a straight bar with both palms facing up.
Keep your upper arms beside your torso, your wrists straight, and your body still.
Bend your elbows as far as you can, then lower the bar under control without turning your forearms.

name: Neutral-Grip Rope Cable Curl
movementSteps: Stand facing a low cable while holding the rope ends with both palms facing inward.
Keep your upper arms beside your torso, your wrists straight, and your body still.
Bend your elbows as far as you can, then return under control without turning your forearms.

name: Pronated Straight-Bar Cable Curl
movementSteps: Stand facing a low cable while holding a straight bar with both palms facing down.
Keep your upper arms beside your torso, your wrists straight, and your body still.
Bend your elbows as far as you can, then lower the bar under control without turning your forearms.

name: Two-Dumbbell Farmer Carry
movementSteps: Log the weight of one dumbbell, not the combined pair.
Hold one equal-weight dumbbell in each hand without straps or hooks.
Keep your upper arms at your sides, your palms facing your thighs, and your elbows straight.
Walk continuously forward on a level surface for the set time while keeping your shoulders controlled and your torso upright.
Avoid turning, marching in place, or converting the carry into another exercise.

name: Repetitive Grip-Trainer Close
movementSteps: Hold one 30 kg-rated grip trainer in one hand without assistance from the other hand.
Close and release the fingers under control for 30 repeated grip cycles.
Close the handles only as far as you comfortably can, and use a steady pace and comfortable arm position.
Complete three sets, log each set separately, and repeat with the other hand.
Enter no lifted weight because the trainer's rating is non-comparable product resistance.

name: Seated Dumbbell Forearm Pronation
movementSteps: Sit with the working shoulder relaxed, the elbow bent about 90 degrees, and the forearm supported on a table.
Begin with the palm facing up while holding a plate-loaded dumbbell vertically.
Turn only the forearm until the thumb points upward.
Return under control without moving the wrist, elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Seated Dumbbell Forearm Supination
movementSteps: Sit with your working shoulder relaxed, your elbow bent about 90 degrees, and your forearm supported on a table.
Begin with your palm facing down while holding a plate-loaded dumbbell vertically.
Turn only your forearm until your thumb points upward.
Return under control without moving your wrist, elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Pressure-Biofeedback Side-Lying Hip Abduction
movementSteps: Lie on one side on a treatment table with the working leg on top, both hips facing straight ahead, the lower leg bent for stability, and a cuff weight secured just above the working ankle.
Place a pressure-biofeedback unit beneath your torso, inflate it to 40 mmHg, and keep it between 35 and 45 mmHg while a horizontal band marks the 35-degree stopping point.
Keep the pelvis and spine still, the working knee straight, and the toes pointing forward.
Raise the straight top leg directly out to the side until it contacts the stopping band.
Lower the leg under control without rolling the pelvis or turning the toes upward.

name: Supported Standing Band Hip Adduction
movementSteps: Stand upright on the support leg, hold a stable external support with both hands, and secure an elastic band around the working ankle from the side.
Move the straight working leg as far out to the side as is comfortable, keeping tension in the band and the leg slightly behind you.
Keep the pelvis still, the working knee straight, and both sets of toes pointing forward.
Pull the working leg inward without swinging it farther backward, stopping about one foot-width to the side and half a foot-length behind the stance foot.
Return under control along the same side-to-side path, then repeat before changing sides.

name: Prone Table Bent-Knee Hip Extension
movementSteps: Lie face down with your torso and pelvis supported on a table and your working thigh hanging beyond its edge.
Keep your working knee bent at 90 degrees and begin with your thigh angled 30 degrees downward.
Keep your pelvis and back still as you lift the thigh until it reaches 5 degrees behind your body.
Lower your thigh under control without changing the knee angle or moving through your back or pelvis.

name: Therapist-Held Supine Band Hip External Rotation
movementSteps: Lie on your back on a treatment table with both thighs supported over the wedge so your hips stay bent at 30 degrees and your knees stay bent.
Secure the elastic band at the working ankle.
Have the therapist hold the working knee against the support and pull the other end of the band against the movement.
Keep your pelvis and back still, and begin with the working thigh pointing straight ahead.
Move the working lower leg inward against the band until you reach the middle of your comfortable range.
Return to the straight-ahead position without lifting or turning the working thigh, and finish the set before changing sides.

name: Bodyweight Active Straight-Leg Raise
movementSteps: Lie on your back with your torso and pelvis supported on a table and both legs straight.
Keep the other leg supported and the working knee straight.
Raise the working leg as far as you can while keeping the knee straight, then lower it under control.
Keep the effort centered on the working hip without deliberately adding spinal, pelvic, or knee motion.

name: 25% Body-Mass Barbell Good Morning
aliases: Barbell Good Morning at 25% Body Mass
movementSteps: Stand upright with your feet approximately shoulder-width apart and naturally turned slightly outward.
Place a free bar securely across the back of your shoulders and upper back in a comfortable hand position.
Keep your head aligned with your spine, brace your trunk, and keep both feet planted.
Load the bar with 25 percent of your body weight; use 45 lb or 20 kg only if that matches your calculated weight.
Push your hips backward as far as you can while keeping a natural back position and allowing only a small bend in the knees.
Straighten your hips and return to standing at the same controlled speed used for the descent, keeping the bar on your body for all eight repetitions.

name: Seated Flywheel Hip Internal Rotation
movementSteps: Sit on a hydraulic treatment table set 75 cm above the floor with both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, both feet hanging freely, your hands crossed over your shoulders, and your pelvis centered.
Secure the lower end of the working thigh with one belt and place two belts across the front points of your hip bones to hold your pelvis still.

Connect the working ankle brace to the Conic Power Move cable with a carabiner. Set the wall-mounted flywheel 7 cm above the floor in the upper-middle frame position, attach the 460 g load 15 cm from the center, and adjust the cable so your hip can move through its full comfortable range.
Turn the working thigh inward as fast as possible so the lower leg moves outward while the pelvis stays still.
Return while resisting the flywheel's pull, keeping the knee angle fixed and avoiding movement through the pelvis or back.
Complete two sets of ten progressively harder warm-up repetitions, then perform three progressive repetitions and seven high-intensity work repetitions.
Repeat the same setup for the other leg and log it as a separate set.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
movementSteps: Sit with the upper back anchored against a 35.5-centimeter bench and a padded barbell across the pelvis.
Plant your feet at shoulder width so your knees finish near 90 degrees, and steady the bar with your palms facing up.
Raise the pelvis until the hips reach neutral.
Lower until the plates return to the floor without arching your back or letting your knees drift outward.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
movementSteps: Lie with your upper back firmly on the floor, a padded barbell across your hips, your feet shoulder-width apart, and your knees bent near 115 degrees.
Steady the bar with your palms facing up.
Raise your pelvis until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, with your knees bent near 115 degrees.
Lower until the plates return to the floor without shifting your upper torso, arching your back, or letting your knees drift outward.

name: Barbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Lie on a flat bench with the eyes beneath the racked bar and the feet planted.
Lower the bar under control toward the lower chest.
Press the bar upward until your elbows are straight.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell beside each side of the chest.
Press both dumbbells upward until your elbows are straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control while keeping the forearms beneath the loads.

name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Lie on a flat bench holding the dumbbells beside the chest with the palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows closer to your torso and press until your arms are straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control while keeping your palms facing each other.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
movementSteps: Position a flat bench so the Smith bar descends toward the lower chest.
Unrack the bar and lower it under control along the rails.
Press until your elbows are straight without allowing your shoulders to lift from the bench.

name: Machine Chest Press
movementSteps: Adjust the seat so the neutral-grip handles begin beside the mid-chest with the forearms aligned to the machine path.
Keep your torso against the pad as you press the handles forward and slightly inward until your elbows are straight.
Return the handles under control.

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
movementSteps: Stand between two chest-height cable handles in a stable staggered stance with the palms facing inward.
Press both handles forward while allowing your shoulder blades to move naturally around your ribs.
Return until the elbows pass slightly behind the torso without rotating the trunk.

name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
movementSteps: Stand with one chest-height cable handle beside the working side of your chest and your palm facing inward.
Keep your torso from twisting as you press the handle forward and straighten your arm, allowing the working shoulder blade to move naturally.
Return under control before changing sides.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell beside the working side of your chest and your palm facing inward.
Keep your torso square against the weight on one side as you press until your arm is straight.
Lower the dumbbell under control before changing sides.

name: Push-Up
movementSteps: Begin in a straight-body plank with the hands slightly wider than the shoulders.
Lower the chest toward the floor without losing trunk position.
Press your body away by straightening your elbows and letting your shoulder blades move naturally around your ribs.

name: Knee Push-Up
movementSteps: Begin with the knees and hands supporting the body and maintain a straight line from the knees through the shoulders.
Lower the chest toward the floor while maintaining that straight line.
Press away until your elbows are straight, letting your shoulder blades move naturally around your ribs.

name: Barbell Floor Press
movementSteps: Lie on the floor beneath a safely positioned bar with the knees bent.
Lower the bar until the upper arms contact the floor without bouncing.
Pause briefly, then press upward until your elbows are straight.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
movementSteps: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell beside each side of the chest, the palms facing inward, and the knees bent.
Lower the dumbbells until the upper arms contact the floor without bouncing.
Press both dumbbells upward until your elbows are straight.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and lie with the feet planted and the eyes below the racked bar.
Lower the bar under control toward the upper chest.
Press the bar upward until your elbows are straight without lifting your shoulders from the bench.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
movementSteps: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and lie with one dumbbell beside each upper-chest line.
Keep each forearm beneath its dumbbell as you press upward and slightly inward until your elbows are straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control without letting the upper arms drift into a vertical shoulder-press path.

name: Incline Smith Machine Bench Press
movementSteps: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and position it so the Smith bar descends toward the upper chest without forcing the shoulders forward.
Lower the bar along the rails under control.
Press until your elbows are straight while keeping your torso and shoulders supported.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
movementSteps: Adjust the seat so the handles begin beside the upper chest and follow an approximately 30-degree upward path relative to a horizontal press.
Keep your torso against the pad as you press the handles forward and upward until your elbows are straight.
Return the handles under control.

name: Reclined Unilateral Machine Leg Extension
movementSteps: Sit in a single-leg knee-extension machine with the backrest reclined so your hip is bent near 40 degrees.
Align your knee with the machine's pivot and place the lower shin against the pad.
Keep your pelvis, back, hip, ankle, and foot still as you straighten the knee completely.
Return under control.

name: Upright Unilateral Machine Leg Extension
movementSteps: Sit upright in a single-leg knee-extension machine with your hip bent near 90 degrees.
Align your knee with the machine's pivot and place the lower shin against the pad.
Keep your pelvis, back, hip, ankle, and foot still as you straighten the knee completely.
Return under control.

name: Seated Unilateral Machine Leg Curl
movementSteps: Sit in a single-leg curl machine with your hip bent near 90 degrees and your pelvis secured to the pad.
Align your knee with the machine's pivot and place the lower part of your leg against the pad.
Keep your pelvis, back, hip, ankle, and foot still as you bend your knee from straight to approximately 90 degrees.
Return under control.

name: Prone Unilateral Machine Leg Curl
movementSteps: Lie face down in a single-leg curl machine with your hip bent near 30 degrees and your pelvis secured to the pad.
Align your knee with the machine's pivot and place the lower part of your leg against the pad.
Keep your pelvis, back, hip, ankle, and foot still as you bend your knee from straight to approximately 90 degrees.
Return under control.

name: Standing Single-Arm Landmine Press Power Test
movementSteps: Fix one end of an Olympic bar in a landmine pivot and count the full bar plus every plate as the logged load.
For the right arm, stand with the left foot forward and both sets of toes pointing ahead; mirror the stance for the left arm.
Grip the moving end of the bar firmly and begin with it close to your working shoulder.
Press the sleeve through its pivoted arc to a controlled end range without deliberately driving through the hips, knees, or ankles, then return it to the shoulder.
Keep your torso and hips controlled throughout the movement.
Perform three power-focused repetitions and log the opposite side separately.

name: Barbell Push Press
movementSteps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold a straight barbell across the front of your shoulders with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width.
Brace your torso and make a quick, shallow dip by bending your hips and knees while keeping both feet on the floor.
Immediately drive through your feet and straighten your hips and knees to send the bar upward.
Press the bar in front of your head until your arms are straight overhead, allowing your shoulder blades to move naturally.
Finish standing with your elbows straight without dipping under the bar.
Lower the bar under control to the front rack.

name: Prone Dumbbell Reverse Fly
movementSteps: Lie face down on a bench with one dumbbell in each hand, your palms facing inward, and your elbows held in a fixed slight bend.
Sweep your upper arms out at shoulder height until they line up with your torso, keeping your shoulder blades controlled instead of deliberately pinching them together.
Lower under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or rotating the shoulders.

name: Standing Band Reverse Fly
movementSteps: Stand upright holding an elastic band in front of the chest with the palms facing inward and the elbows in a fixed slight bend.
Brace your torso and sweep your upper arms outward at shoulder height to stretch the band, keeping your shoulder blades controlled instead of deliberately pinching them together.
Return under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or rotating the shoulders.

name: Neutral-Grip Machine Reverse Fly
movementSteps: Sit facing the reverse-fly machine pad, and hold the handles with the palms facing each other, the upper arms at shoulder height, and the elbows in a fixed slight bend.
Follow the lever path to sweep your upper arms outward, keeping your shoulder blades controlled instead of deliberately pinching them together.
Return under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or adding shoulder rotation.

name: Pronated-Grip Machine Reverse Fly
movementSteps: Sit facing the reverse-fly machine pad, and hold the horizontal handles with the palms facing down, the upper arms at shoulder height, and the elbows in a fixed slight bend.
Follow the lever path to sweep your upper arms outward, keeping your shoulder blades controlled instead of deliberately pinching them together.
Return under control without rowing, changing the elbow bend, or deliberately turning your upper arms outward.

name: Standing Band Scapular Depression
movementSteps: Stand tall holding the overhead-anchored band beside the working thigh with your elbow straight and the band just taut.
Pull the working shoulder blade down against the band for two seconds without moving the arm.
Return for two seconds without bending your elbow, moving your arm at the shoulder, leaning your torso, or moving your neck.
Rest five seconds between repetitions.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shrug
movementSteps: Stand tall holding one dumbbell beside your body with your elbow straight and your thumb pointing forward.
Shrug the working shoulder blade toward your ear while keeping your upper arm at your side.
Lower under control without rolling the shoulder, bending the elbow, moving the neck, or leaning the trunk.

name: Bilateral 30-Degree Stabilization Shrug
movementSteps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and both arms raised 30 degrees out to the sides.
Lightly touch the thumb-side edges of your wrists against the plastic guides, use the angle gauge to keep your arms in place, and have a partner steady your chin and upper chest.
Shrug both shoulder blades to your personal maximum-height target bars, and hold the top position for five seconds.
Lower slowly without bending the elbows, moving the neck or trunk, or adding external load.
Perform two attempts.
Record the larger shoulder-blade angle measured immediately after each hold; do not try to track the angle while moving.

name: Supine Dumbbell Scapular Punch
movementSteps: Lie on your back with one dumbbell held vertically above your shoulder, your upper arm pointing straight up, and your elbow straight.
Reach the dumbbell toward the ceiling by letting your shoulder blade slide forward around your ribs without bending your elbow or lifting the arm farther.
Return under control without adding a press.

name: Standing Band Scapular Retraction
movementSteps: Stand facing a low band anchor and hold your working arm almost straight ahead with your elbow straight and the band just taut.
Pull your working shoulder blade back toward your spine against the band for two seconds.
Return for two seconds without bending your elbow, moving your arm at the shoulder, shrugging, turning your torso, or moving your neck.
Rest five seconds between repetitions.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise
movementSteps: Stand upright with one dumbbell beside your thigh, your palm facing your body, and your elbow nearly straight.
Raise your upper arm directly out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Avoid shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive.
Lower the dumbbell under control.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
movementSteps: Stand upright holding one cable handle with the pulley aligned approximately with your working hand in the arm-at-side start.
Keep your palm facing your body and your elbow nearly straight.
Raise your upper arm directly out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Lower the handle under control without shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive.

name: Barbell Pullover
movementSteps: Lie on your back along a flat bench and hold a straight bar over your chest with your palms facing forward and your elbows nearly straight.
Keep your elbow angle fixed as you lower the bar behind your head as far as you comfortably can.
Bring your arms back over your chest while keeping the same elbow angle.
Do not turn the movement into a triceps exercise by bending and straightening your elbows.

name: Shoulder-Width Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
movementSteps: Stand facing a high cable and hold a straight bar at shoulder width with your palms facing down and your elbows nearly straight.
Begin with your hands overhead and brace your torso.
Keep your elbow angle fixed as you bring the bar down to your thighs.
Return overhead under control without rowing or bending your elbows.

name: Wide-Grip Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
movementSteps: Stand facing a high cable and hold a straight bar wider than shoulder width with your palms facing down and your elbows nearly straight.
Begin with your hands overhead and brace your torso.
Keep your elbow angle fixed as you bring the bar down to your thighs.
Return overhead under control without rowing or bending your elbows.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
movementSteps: Stand holding a barbell at shoulder width with your palms facing back.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is inclined, then brace without changing the torso angle.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs while your elbows travel back near your torso.
Lower the bar under control.

name: Underhand Barbell Row
movementSteps: Hold a barbell at shoulder width with your palms facing forward.
Maintain a strict hip hinge with your trunk braced.
Keep your elbows tucked as you pull the bar toward your lower torso without standing up.
Lower the bar under control.

name: Pendlay Row
movementSteps: Set a barbell on the floor, hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing back, and bend forward from your hips.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs without standing up or arching your back.
Lower the bar to a complete floor reset.
Rebrace before the next repetition.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
movementSteps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inward.
Establish a strict hip hinge and hold your trunk angle steady.
Pull both dumbbells toward the sides of your lower torso while keeping your elbows close.
Lower the dumbbells without changing your trunk angle.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
movementSteps: Place your opposite hand and knee on a bench while the foot on your working side stays planted.
Hold one dumbbell with your palm facing inward and keep your hips level and facing forward.
Pull your working elbow toward your hip without rotating your torso.
Lower the dumbbell under control.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
movementSteps: Lie face down with your chest supported on an incline bench and hold two dumbbells with your palms facing inward.
Let your shoulder blades move around your rib cage.
Pull your elbows toward your lower torso.
Lower the dumbbells under control.

name: Seated Cable Row
movementSteps: Sit upright at a low cable station holding a narrow parallel handle with your palms facing each other, and keep your torso steady without back support.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs while keeping your elbows tucked.
Return the handle until your shoulder blades move forward under control.

name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Row
movementSteps: Sit upright at a low cable station and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
Brace your trunk and keep your pelvis square.
Pull your working elbow toward your hip.
Return your arm forward without rotating your torso.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
movementSteps: Sit at a linked-arm row machine with your chest against the pad and hold the handles with your palms facing each other.
Let your shoulder blades move naturally as you drive your elbows toward your lower ribs.
Keep your chest against the pad.
Return the linked lever under control.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Machine Row
movementSteps: Sit against the chest pad of a single-arm row machine and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
Keep your pelvis and chest square as you pull your working elbow toward your lower torso.
Return the lever without twisting away from the pad.

name: Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
movementSteps: Set the Smith bar near knee height and hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing back.
Establish a strict hip hinge beneath the rail path.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs without changing your torso angle.
Lower the bar along the rails under control.

name: Inverted Row
movementSteps: Lie beneath a fixed straight bar, hold it at shoulder width with your palms facing away from you, and keep your feet on the floor with your body nearly parallel to it.
Keep a straight line from your shoulders through your heels.
Pull your chest toward the bar while letting your shoulder blades move naturally.
Lower your body under control.

name: Standing Cable External Rotation
movementSteps: Stand sideways to the cable, keep the working upper arm beside your body, and bend the elbow about 90 degrees.
Rotate the forearm away from the abdomen.
Return under control without moving the elbow, pinching the shoulder blade back, or turning your torso.

name: Standing Band External Rotation
movementSteps: Stand side-on with the band anchored across the body and a towel roll between the working upper arm and torso.
Keep the elbow bent about 90 degrees as you turn the forearm away from your stomach against the band.
Return without moving the elbow, shoulder blade, or torso.

name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
movementSteps: Lie on the side you are not exercising, with a towel roll between your working upper arm and torso.
Bend the elbow about 90 degrees and hold a dumbbell above your stomach.
Rotate the forearm toward the ceiling.
Lower the dumbbell under control without lifting the upper arm, rolling your torso, or pinching the shoulder blade back.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Front Raise
movementSteps: Stand upright with one dumbbell beside your thigh, your palm facing your body, and your elbow nearly straight.
Raise the upper arm directly forward from the side to shoulder height without bending the elbow, shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive.
Lower the arm under control.

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Hold a barbell with a wide overhand grip and keep your body bent forward from the hips.
Pull toward the upper chest while the elbows travel out at shoulder height.
Pinch your shoulder blades together without pulling them down.
Lower the bar without standing up or arching your back.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Lie face down with your chest supported on an incline bench and hold two dumbbells with your palms facing inward.
Keep the forearms beneath the elbows as the upper arms travel out at shoulder height.
Pinch your shoulder blades together, then lower the dumbbells under control without lifting your chest.

name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Sit upright at a shoulder-height cable and hold a wide straight attachment with your palms facing down.
Brace the unsupported torso as you pull toward the upper chest with the elbows flared at shoulder height.
Pinch your shoulder blades together, then return under control.

name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Sit upright at a shoulder-height cable and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
Keep the pelvis and torso square as the working elbow travels out and back at shoulder height.
Pull the working shoulder blade toward your spine, then return without turning your torso.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Sit at a horizontal row machine with your chest against the pad and hold the wide handles with your palms facing down.
Pull with both elbows out at shoulder height while letting your shoulder blades pinch together naturally.
Return the linked lever under control.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Machine Rear-Delt Row
movementSteps: Sit against the chest pad of a single-arm horizontal row machine and hold one handle with your palm facing inward.
Keep the pelvis and chest square while the working elbow travels out and back at shoulder height.
Pull the working shoulder blade toward your spine, then return the handle without twisting.

name: Standing Cable Internal Rotation
movementSteps: Stand side-on with the cable anchored outside the working shoulder and a towel roll between the upper arm and torso.
Keep the elbow bent about 90 degrees, and turn the forearm across your stomach.
Return under control without moving the elbow, reaching the shoulder blade forward, or turning your torso.

name: Standing Band Internal Rotation
movementSteps: Stand side-on with the band anchored outside the working shoulder and a towel roll between the upper arm and torso.
Keep the elbow bent about 90 degrees, and turn the forearm across your stomach against the band.
Return without moving the elbow, reaching the shoulder blade forward, or turning your torso.

name: MedX Isolated Lumbar Extension
movementSteps: Sit in the MedX lower-back machine with your thighs at a right angle to the seat.
Tighten the thigh restraint, secure the leg restraint just above your kneecaps, and tighten the footboard.
Keep your upper hips against the rolling restraint and push only against the pad behind your upper torso.
Straighten your back for at least two seconds, moving from the machine's 72-degree curled-forward mark to its 0-degree upright mark.
Hold the upright position for one second.
Return for at least four seconds without lifting or turning your hips or pushing with your legs.

name: 30-Degree Curl-Up
movementSteps: Lie on your back in a stable position with your hips held still.
Begin with your torso resting on the floor.
Curl your head, shoulders, and upper back about 30 degrees off the floor without lifting from your hips.
Lower to the starting position under control without turning the repetition into a full sit-up.

name: Fixed-Leg Side-Lying Lateral Trunk Lift
movementSteps: Lie on one side with your torso resting on the floor, cross your top foot over the lower leg, and secure that foot firmly.
Keep your hips still so the lift comes from your side rather than from pushing through the hip.
Lift your upper body sideways until it is about 30 degrees off the floor.
Lower to the starting position under control.
Repeat on the other side and log it separately.

name: Seated Machine Torso Twist
movementSteps: Sit in a horizontal torso-twist machine with the feet behind the ankle rollers, the shoulder pads in contact, and both hands holding the separate handles at shoulder height.
Hold the pelvis against the seat and keep the hips and legs still.
For one logged direction, begin rotated left and drive the shoulder pads from left to right in a controlled motion.
Turn as far as feels comfortable, then return to the left-facing start under control.
Reset the machine, repeat the same movement from right to left, and log that direction separately.
Treat the right-to-left direction as a mirrored training adaptation and do not alternate directions within a repetition.

name: Barbell Split Squat
movementSteps: Place a barbell securely across your upper back and hold it with both palms facing forward.
Take a split stance about as long as the distance from the outside of your hip to the outside of your ankle, with your front foot flat and the ball of your rear foot on the floor.
Keep that stance length throughout the set, using a comfortable position for each foot.
Keep your torso erect and both foot contacts fixed as you lower until your lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
Push through your front foot and straighten the front hip and knee to rise back to the split stance.
Finish in the same split stance without stepping between repetitions.

name: 21 cm Bodyweight Forward Step-Up
movementSteps: Stand facing a platform exactly 21 centimeters above the lower floor with the lead foot placed fully on top and the trail foot on the lower floor.
Shift onto the lead leg without pushing or hopping from the trail leg.
Push through the lead foot and straighten that hip and knee until the other foot reaches the platform beside it.
Pause briefly with both feet on the platform.
Shift back onto the lead leg, return the trail foot to the lower floor, and step the lead foot down beside it to complete the repetition.
Replace the same lead foot fully on the platform before the next repetition, and switch lead sides after the set.

name: Single-Dumbbell Suitcase Carry
movementSteps: Log the weight of the single dumbbell.
Hold the dumbbell beside one thigh with your palm facing inward and your elbow straight.
Use no straps or hooks.
Walk continuously forward on a level surface for the set time, staying upright without leaning away from the dumbbell.
Log the other side as well.
Do not turn, march in place, walk backward, or lean deliberately to create repetitions.

name: Standing Low-Cable Upright Row
movementSteps: Stand at a low cable with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the straight bar with the overhand hand spacing shown for the exercise, keep your torso upright, and brace your core.
Pull the bar straight up, bending your elbows and raising your upper arms out and slightly forward.
Keep your elbows slightly above your hands and stop when they reach shoulder height.
Lower the bar slowly without adding a shrug, pinching your shoulder blades together, turning your upper arms, leaning, or pushing with your legs.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
Brace your trunk without leaning back and keep your hips and knees motionless.
Press the bar overhead, letting your shoulder blades move naturally, and move your head only enough to clear the bar.
Finish with your elbows straight and the bar balanced over the middle of your feet.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.

name: Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward and your elbows slightly forward of your torso.
Brace your trunk and keep your hips and knees motionless.
Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without turning your hands or leaning back, and let your shoulder blades move naturally.
Finish with your elbows straight and the weights balanced over your body.
Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at the shoulder you are working, with your palm facing forward and your elbow slightly forward.
Brace your torso, keep your hips level and facing forward, and do not bend your hips or knees.
Press the dumbbell overhead on a slightly forward path without turning your hand, leaning sideways or back, or twisting, and let your shoulder blade move naturally.
Finish with your elbow straight and the weight balanced over your body.
Lower the dumbbell under control before changing sides.

name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Set the bench backrest to about 85 degrees and sit with your pelvis and upper torso supported and your feet planted.
Hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward and your elbows slightly forward of your torso.
Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without turning your hands, pushing through your legs, or lifting your torso from the bench.
Let your shoulder blades move as much as the backrest allows, and finish with your elbows straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Set a bench backrest to about 80 degrees inside a rack and sit with your pelvis and upper torso supported and your feet planted.
Unrack the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
Press the bar overhead in front of your head without pushing through your legs or lifting your torso from the bench, and let your shoulder blades move naturally.
Finish with your elbows straight.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.

name: Unsupported Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
aliases: Seated Dumbbell Press Without Back Support
movementSteps: Sit upright on a flat bench without a backrest, plant your feet, and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward.
Brace your trunk so your ribs stay stacked over your pelvis.
Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without leaning back, pushing through your legs, or turning your hands.
Finish with your elbows straight.
Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Set the bench backrest to about 75 degrees and sit with your upper torso and pelvis supported and your feet planted.
Hold one dumbbell at the shoulder you are working with your palm facing inward.
Press the dumbbell overhead on a slightly forward path without turning your hand, pushing through your legs, twisting, or leaning sideways, while keeping both hips on the bench.
Finish with your elbow straight and lower under control.
Repeat on the other side.

name: Single-Arm Standing Kettlebell Overhead Press
movementSteps: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold one kettlebell at your working shoulder with your wrist straight and the bell resting against your forearm.
Brace your trunk and keep your hips and knees motionless.
Press the kettlebell overhead on a slightly forward path without letting it flip upside down, leaning, or twisting.
Finish with your elbow straight and your forearm vertical.
Lower the kettlebell under control to the rack before changing sides.

name: Seated Smith Machine Overhead Press
movementSteps: Place an upright bench under the Smith bar so the rails keep the bar in front of your head, set the backrest to about 85 degrees, and sit with your torso supported and your feet planted.
Unhook the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
Press along the rails without pushing through your legs or lifting from the bench.
Finish with your elbows straight.
Lower the bar under control and rehook it securely.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
movementSteps: Adjust the seat so the handles begin near shoulder height with your palms facing each other, then sit against the machine pad with your feet planted.
Press both lever arms overhead along their converging front paths without pushing through your legs or lifting from the pad.
Finish with your elbows straight without forcing your shoulders forward.
Return the handles under control.

name: Wall-Supported Strict Handstand Push-Up
movementSteps: Place the handstand supports 10 cm from a wall and 20 cm wider than your shoulders, with a 15 cm sponge centered beneath your head.
Kick up into a handstand and let only your feet touch the wall gently.
Lower until your head contacts the sponge.
Press until your arms are straight overhead without folding at your waist, bending your knees, swinging for momentum, or pushing off the wall.
Perform as many controlled repetitions as you can in 40 seconds; five repetitions is only a suggested starting target.
Count only repetitions that follow the setup and movement rules above.

name: Pull-Up
movementSteps: Hang from a fixed bar with your palms facing away, your hands shoulder-width apart, your elbows straight, and your torso braced.
Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the bar, without swinging or using the hips or legs.
Lower under control to a full hang.

name: Chin-Up
movementSteps: Hang from a fixed bar with your palms facing you, your hands shoulder-width apart, your elbows straight, and your torso braced.
Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the bar, without swinging or lower-body drive.
Return under control to a full hang.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
movementSteps: Hang from parallel handles with the palms facing each other, straight elbows, and the trunk braced.
Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the handles, keeping the lower body motionless.
Lower under control to a full hang.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
movementSteps: Hang from a fixed bar with your palms facing away, your hands wider than shoulder width, your elbows straight, and your torso braced.
Pull your body upward until your chin clears the bar without swinging or pushing with your lower body.
Lower under control to a full hang.

name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
movementSteps: Set the assistance load, kneel or stand on the machine platform, and hold the handles at shoulder width with your palms facing away and your elbows straight.
Pull until the chin clears the handles without kicking or leaning.
Lower under control while the platform guides the body vertically.

name: Assisted Chin-Up Machine
movementSteps: Set the assistance load, kneel or stand on the guided platform, and hold the handles at shoulder width with your palms facing you and your elbows straight.
Pull until the chin clears the handles without kicking or leaning.
Lower under control to the starting position.

name: Cable Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit at a cable pulldown station with your thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold the bar with a medium-width grip and your palms facing forward.
Keep the trunk braced and nearly upright as you pull the bar in front of the head toward the upper chest by driving the elbows down.
Return overhead under control.

name: Close-Grip Neutral Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit with the thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold a close parallel-grip attachment with the palms facing each other.
Keep the torso braced, and drive the elbows down as the handle travels in front of the head toward the upper chest.
Return overhead under control.

name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit with your thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold the bar at shoulder width with your palms facing you.
Hold the trunk nearly upright, and drive the elbows down and back as the bar travels in front of the head toward the upper chest.
Return overhead under control.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit with your thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold the bar wider than shoulder width with your palms facing forward.
Keep the trunk braced and nearly upright as you pull the bar in front of the head by driving the elbows down until the bar approaches the upper chest.
Return overhead under control.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit with your thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold one high-cable handle with your palm facing inward.
Keep the shoulders and pelvis square as you drive the working elbow down beside the ribs without rotating or leaning.
Return the arm overhead under control.

name: Machine Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit in the pulldown machine with your thighs secured beneath the pad, and hold the overhead handles with your palms facing each other.
Keep the torso braced, and drive both elbows down as the levers follow their guided path.
Return to full overhead reach under control.

name: Single-Arm Machine Lat Pulldown
movementSteps: Sit in the single-arm pulldown machine with your thighs secured, and hold one overhead handle with your palm facing inward.
Keep the torso and pelvis square as you drive the working elbow down without rotating or leaning.
Return the lever overhead under control.

name: Seated Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
movementSteps: Sit astride a flat bench with both forearms supported, palms facing down, and your hands just beyond the edge.
Hold a straight bar without opening your fingers, and lift both hands as far as you can with control.
Lower under control without rotating the forearms or moving the elbows, shoulders, or torso.

name: Seated Barbell Wrist Curl
movementSteps: Sit astride a flat bench with both forearms supported, palms facing up, and your hands just beyond the edge.
Hold a straight bar without opening the fingers.
Curl both hands upward as far as you can with control.
Lower the bar under control without rotating the forearms or moving the elbows, shoulders, or torso.

name: Standing Dumbbell Radial Deviation
movementSteps: Stand tall with your working arm beside your body, your elbow straight, and your thumb pointing forward.
Grip below the dumbbell's bottom collar with its shaft pointing ahead.
Raise the thumb side of your wrist through the controlled available range.
Lower under control without rotating your forearm or moving your elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Standing Dumbbell Ulnar Deviation
movementSteps: Stand tall with your working arm beside your body, your elbow straight, and your thumb pointing forward.
Grip just above the dumbbell's bottom collar with its shaft pointing behind.
Raise the little-finger side of the wrist through the controlled available range.
Lower without rotating the forearm or moving the elbow, shoulder, or torso.
